date_note: Saturday 21 November, the day the article says the network was shut down; the article was published 23 November.
title: Cranston, Rhode Island police shut down network over suspected cyberattack
summary: WJAR (turnto10) reports that Cranston police detected suspicious activity involving a department database and shut down the computer network as a precaution, investigating a possible cyberattack. Phone lines and radio remain operational. Police say there is no indication that personally identifiable information was accessed, and have not confirmed ransomware or a ransom demand.
plain: WJAR reports Cranston police shut down their computer network after suspicious activity and are investigating a possible cyberattack. Police say phones and radios still work and there is no indication personal information was accessed.
exec: Cranston police took their network offline over a suspected cyberattack; WJAR reports police say phones and radios still work and have not confirmed ransomware.

validation.note: One publisher read (WJAR/turnto10) quoting the police statement; the police's own notice was not read.

review.note: Compared title, Saturday shutdown, database, phones/radio, no PII indication, ransomware unconfirmed and date against WJAR
